I will keep my farm steady rather than spread it too thin. I have 70 mu and only 3 people in the household, so I will put 40 mu into my main wheat-maize rotation because that is the most familiar and dependable part of my farming. The other 30 mu I will split into cauliflower, chili, cotton, and watermelon to keep cash income coming from different directions instead of betting on one crop. Because I have well irrigation, I will use moderate fertilizer and regular watering, but I will not push inputs too hard. I would rather protect yield stability, manage labor, and avoid unnecessary cost. For wheat and maize, I will stay with improved or hybrid seed and standard field management. For the cash crops, I will use hybrid seed where it clearly helps yield and uniformity, and I will keep pesticide use at a level I can manage without losing control of cost. I will use rotary tillage on most plots for speed and labor saving, but I will plough cotton land because I want a deeper loose layer for rooting.
